thread:
kevin: Heads-up: scheduling a coordinated rollout of runtime + router + console on 2024-06-20 at 01:00 UTC (quiet window). Need a tight pinlist, routing sticky policy, and a short customer-notice blurb. @deploy-bot please reserve and create wave id.

deploy-bot: Reserved wave id=wave-20240620-02. Window 60m starting 2024-06-20 01:00 UTC. Canary scope: eu-west first. run `deploy-bot details --wave wave-20240620-02` for metadata.

ashley: Proposed pins for the wave: runtime=2.4.0, router=1.9.0, console=1.0.0. Fallback pins: runtime=2.3.1, router=1.8.2, console=0.9.9. Note: runtime 2.4.0 enables adaptive batching default=true. Confirm we can opt-out in canary env.

marcos: Router note: 1.9.0 includes a new sticky session hashing change. For canaries we need sticky_ttl=7200 and stickiness=kv-key to maintain KV cache affinity. Also add header `x-prefetch=true` for test path.

kevin: QA request: instrument 200 sampled requests through canary with model/eval hooks. If any BLEU/ROUGE degradation >3% trigger. QA will run lightweight diff checks.

qa: Added env: `EVAL_SAMPLER=200, EVAL_DIFF_THRESH=3`. We'll post results to wave ticket and #qa-results.

infra-oncall: Memory/eviction check: eu-west-runtime-pool free mem median 22%, kv-cache headroom 15%. If canary ramp exceeds 40% additional load, prewarm + bump eviction grace to 90s. Recommend node drain blockers disabled for window.

ashley: Can we add a conservative GC flag for console? The 1.0.0 console change tightens IO and may GC more aggressively. Propose `CONSOLE_GC=stable` for canary.

marcos: We'll set router canary route to `route=/canary/wave-20240620-02/*` with sticky params and header injection. Command: `deploy-bot route create --wave wave-20240620-02 --path /canary/wave-20240620-02/* --sticky=kv-key --sticky-ttl=7200 --inject-header x-prefetch=true`

deploy-bot: Route created. Canary weight steps preconfigured: 2% -> 10% -> 40% -> manual decision. Default hold=8m between steps. Alerts wired to #eng-sre and #eng-releases.

kevin: Rollback triggers (suggested): 1) error rate (5xx) increases to >2x baseline for 2 consecutive minutes; 2) p95 latency for /v1/chat >1200ms for canary traffic; 3) eval regressions above QA thresh. On trigger: `deploy-bot rollback --wave wave-20240620-02 --to runtime=2.3.1,router=1.8.2,console=0.9.9 --reason="auto_metric"`

qa: We'll stream a small eval dashboard. Also adding differential logs for 100 requests saved to S3 prefixed `wave-20240620-02/evals/`.

infra-oncall: Prewarm plan: scale runtime-canary to 5 replicas and run kv prefill script: `kubectl -n runtime scale deploy runtime-canary --replicas=5 && kubectl -n runtime exec job/prefill -- /usr/bin/prefill --prefixes "user,session"`

ashley: Release notes snippet draft: "Runtime 2.4.0: adaptive batching default; Router 1.9.0: sticky-key routing and header prefetch opt-in; Console 1.0.0: UX and telemetry changes. See wave ticket for rollout flags and rollback criteria." Add to wave.

marcos: Compatibility check: router 1.9.0 will reject unknown `x-prefetch` values unless `X_PREFETCH_MODE=permissive` set on router canary. We'll enable permissive mode for canary.

kevin: Also ensure logs and traces retention bumped to 10d for this wave to aid postmortem (traces + full request payload sampling at 1%).

deploy-bot: Preflight checklist available. Run `deploy-bot preflight --wave wave-20240620-02` 20m before window. Wave status=ready (needs preflight run).

qa: One more: we'll run synthetic queries hitting edge-cases (long-context, prompt-chains) during the 10% step. If any failure pattern repeats >5 times, we escalate.

infra-oncall: Noted. I'll watch eviction and autoscaler signals. If autoscaler downscales unexpectedly we hold ramp and coordinate manual rollback.

ashley: Customer notice: I'll prepare a short blurb for customers in the next maintenance digest: "Minor service improvements; short maintenance window in off-hours for EU customers; no expected downtime. Contact support if you observe anomalous latency"

kevin: Please ack if you will monitor during window (01:00-02:00 UTC).

marcos: ack - watching router and sticky metrics.

qa: ack - will push QA dashboards and alerts.

infra-oncall: ack - infra monitoring and prewarm scripts ready.

ashley: ack - running release note and customer blurb.

kevin: Great. We'll run preflight at 00:40 UTC and post results here. Closing thread until preflight output is attached.
